Only A holds: food factories grew 15.2% (46 to 53) against 10.2% for the rest (215 to 237); B fails (about 2.1x per year compounded and 7x in total, not 3x), C fails (17.6%), and D fails (food stays below hospitals on either extrapolation).

The text does not settle whether studio costs scale with sales (it says only that platform fees move with sales): if every cost stays a fixed share of sales, A wins (0.67 against 0.42 for C), but if studio costs are fixed, a 1% sales rise adds 1.63 - 0.67 = 0.96 and C wins.
